newsitem.title: USA: Calif. tax measure could hurt localities - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Calif. tax measure could hurt localities - Moody's.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service Inc said a tax measure on the California ballot would cast a new shadow over local government debt, but added that it was impossible to fully anticipate its effects.
Moody's said in its Credit Perspectives newsletter dueout Friday that Proposition 218 was, for the municipal finance community, the most significant measure before state voters this November.

The measure would add new limits to the ability of local governments in the state to impose or increase various revenues by establishing new rules for public approval of taxes and levies and by eliminating some assessments outright.

"The provisions of the measure will certainly limit local governments' financial flexibility, but it will take time to determine whether this change results in the weakening of credit quality," Moody's said.
Moody's said, however, that the full impact of the measure may not be known for several years, adding that judicial review may be required to clarify its implications.
"A key risk of the bill is that it could open up a number of issues of California public finance law, resulting in court rulings with unanticipated conclusions and consequences," Moody's said.

Under the proposition, creation of special assessments would be more difficult and their uses more limited, Moody's warned. New requirements for property-related fees and charges could affect revenue bonds in the state, Moody's added.

"Given the difficulty in assessing the magnitude of the measure's impact on local government finance and the lack of consensus regarding the many legal questions raised by the initiative, it would be premature to attempt to identify specific debt issues that would be vulnerable if Proposition 218 were approved," Moody's said.
Moody's said the ratings of affected issuers would be considered on a case-by-case basis.
"This measure would create uncertainty for many California municipalities and outlooks ranging from short-term uncertainty to significantly declining credit quality for some issuers," Moody's said.
